My land is 4.1 mu total. Here in Quzhou, we do wheat first, then maize on the same fields — the whole plot cycles through both. I've been doing this for 15 years, so I know how this land behaves.

**Wheat (winter):** I'll plant in mid-October after preparing the ground with rotary tillage to break down the leftover maize stalks. I use the improved varieties from the county seed shop — Jimai or similar — not hybrid, just improved. Wheat doesn't come in hybrid here. I'll apply base fertilizer before sowing: diammonium phosphate and urea. Then top-dress with urea again at jointing. I irrigate four times: before sowing, before winter sets in, at jointing, and at grain filling. That's standard here. I'll spray herbicide in spring and a fungicide pass later. Should get around 450 jin per mu.

**Maize (summer):** Right after wheat harvest in June, I direct-seed maize — no-tillage, saves time and my son is working in the city so labor is tight. I use Zhengdan 958 or whatever hybrid the local shop is pushing this year. Maize needs more nitrogen, so I apply more. One base application, one topdressing at big bell stage. Summer rains help but I'll irrigate once or twice if it's dry. One herbicide spray, one pesticide spray for corn borer. Yields around 550 jin per mu most years.

The off-farm income gives us some cushion, but I still keep inputs at the level I know works. I don't experiment — small mistakes on 4 mu hurt.
